title: The Book of Philemon Decoded
author: Brittany Johnson
description: The Book of Philemon — every verse decoded into plain, modern English (DMLV).

verses.kjv: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
verses.decoded: Paul, a prisoner for Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dear friend and coworker,

verses.kjv: And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
verses.decoded: and to our loved Apphia, and Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your home:

verses.kjv: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.decoded: May you receive grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,
verses.decoded: I always thank my God when I remember you in my prayers,

verses.kjv: Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;
verses.decoded: because I hear about your love and faith toward the Lord Jesus and all the holy people.

verses.kjv: That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
verses.decoded: I pray that your faith will be active and effective by knowing all the good things we share in Christ Jesus.

verses.kjv: For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
verses.decoded: We have great joy and comfort because of your love, which refreshes the hearts of God’s people, my brother.

verses.kjv: Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
verses.decoded: So even though I could be bold and command you to do what is right in Christ,

verses.kjv: Yet for love's sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
verses.decoded: I prefer to ask you kindly, because of love. I, Paul, an old man now and a prisoner for Jesus Christ,

verses.kjv: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:
verses.decoded: ask you to help my son Onesimus, whom I have fathered while in prison.

verses.kjv: Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:
verses.decoded: He was useless to you before, but now he is useful to both you and me.

verses.kjv: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:
verses.decoded: I am sending him back to you. Please welcome him as if he were my own heart.

verses.kjv: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
verses.decoded: I wanted to keep him with me so he could help me while I am in prison for the gospel,

verses.kjv: But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.
verses.decoded: but I did not want to do anything without your permission. I want you to help him willingly, not because you have to.

verses.kjv: For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;
verses.decoded: Maybe he left you for a while so you could have him back forever.

verses.kjv: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
verses.decoded: He is no longer just a servant, but more than a servant— a dear brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both as a person and as a believer? If you consider me your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.

verses.kjv: If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
verses.decoded: If you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.

verses.kjv: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
verses.decoded: If he has wronged you or owes you anything, charge it to me.

verses.kjv: I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.
verses.decoded: I, Paul, have written this with my own hand; I will pay it back. But I am not even mentioning to you that you owe me your very self besides.

verses.kjv: Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.
verses.decoded: Yes, brother, let me have joy from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in the Lord.

verses.kjv: Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.
verses.decoded: Because I trust that you will obey, I wrote to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.

verses.kjv: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
verses.decoded: But also prepare a place for me to stay, because I hope that through your prayers I will be returned to you.

verses.kjv: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
verses.decoded: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner for Christ Jesus, sends you greetings;

verses.kjv: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.
verses.decoded: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my coworkers.

verses.kjv: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus, a servant.
verses.decoded: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus, a servant.
